AUTOMATIC_FRESH_SESSION and CODEX_DELEGATION are proved end to end with fake executors and, against the installed CLIs, at the contract level only: help flags, authentication, zero-cost probes (empty stdin, --resume with an unknown id) and a dry run. LOCAL_TOOL_FIRST: deterministic tooling runs inside sessions, with `runtime.mjs capture` keeping full output in a log and returning a compact summary. By the security design the supervisor itself runs no command an agent selects.

acceptance.A_structured_checkpoint: agent-runtime/checkpoint@1, validated and kept as authoritative copies in <git common dir>/agent-runtime/<slug>/checkpoints/; tests: coherence, supervisor, simulation
acceptance.B_invalid_checkpoint_never_transitions: rejection, correction in the same session (--resume), at most 2 corrections, then a failed run; tests: 'a rejected checkpoint goes back to the same session…', '…still invalid after the correction limit is never accepted'
acceptance.C_rebuild_without_transcript: bootstrap of a few KB: checkpoint, named authorities, Git state, rules; later sessions never see earlier outputs; tests: bootstrap, simulation ('no transcript or earlier output is carried over')
acceptance.D_terminal_stop: COMPLETED stops all sessions and jobs, is never resolved back open, and an edited state that contradicts the event log is refused; tests: supervisor, simulation, security
acceptance.E_codex_optional_accelerator: Codex job in its own worktree and branch, verified independently of Codex's report, judged and integrated by the next Claude unit; test: the three-phase simulation
acceptance.F_codex_failure_does_not_block: unavailable, quota, invalid handoff, changes outside allowed paths, ignored-material changes or a rewritten .git all hand the work back to the next Claude unit; tests: simulation, guards
acceptance.G_git_worktree_safety: preflight (branch, history, unknown changes, remote), no destructive Git, hardened Git invocation (attributes, fsmonitor, hooks, signing policy, pinned git dir, remote checks outside any repository); tests: supervisor, guards, security, hardening
acceptance.H_no_founder_relay: the supervisor starts every session and job and carries every hand-over; the Founder only starts a mission, resumes after a pause, resolves BLOCKED/FOUNDER_REQUIRED and adopts reviewed agent configuration
acceptance.I_no_gate_weakened: findings, blockers, do_not_reopen, invariants and freezes cannot be dropped between sessions; CLOSED_NOT_READY names a blocker; READY states keep none open; a blocker closes only with evidence; the mission's own gates and judges are untouched

conditions.condition: one supervisor per mission, started by hand; two supervisors racing for the same stale lock could both start
conditions.trigger: before supervisors are ever started automatically or on a schedule: replace the lock takeover with an atomic rename-based one, with a test

conditions.condition: session results, Codex logs and captured logs can contain whatever a worker printed, secrets included; they stay local and gitignored
conditions.trigger: never attach .agent-runtime/ wholesale to a pull request or to evidence; redact or check a log by hand before sharing it

observations: The supervisor's signing policy reads the Founder's --global config only; a commit.gpgsign set in the system config would not be followed (not the case today; documented).
The submodule, gc and maintenance switches are defence in depth without a dedicated test.
limitations: Start the supervisor from a terminal, in the main checkout or another checkout no mission session works in; it refuses mission and job worktrees.
Checkpoints happen at semantic boundaries; the installed CLI gives an external process no reliable live context-size signal, and an over-long unit relies on Claude Code's auto-compaction.
A hung session is never killed automatically; stop the supervisor and run again.
The Claude Pro plan's usage limit ends a session without a checkpoint: one retry, then PAUSED until the same command is run again.
Deterministic commands longer than ten minutes run inside a session (in the background, or split); the supervisor runs none.
Removing a mission worktree removes its session workspace; the control state and the event log stay in the Git common directory.
